newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MONTREAL STUMBLES BUT RALLIES TO BEAT DALLAS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MONTREAL STUMBLES BUT RALLIES TO BEAT DALLAS.

text.p: Brian Savage and Patrice Brisebois scored 2:16 apart in the third period as the Montreal Canadiens blew a lead but rallied for a 6-4 victory over the Dallas Stars on Wednesday.
Turner Stevenson added his first goal of the season for the Canadiens.
Joe Nieuwendyk scored twice in 1:45 early in the third period for Dallas, which lost its third straight game.

At Florida, Guy Hebert made 28 saves for his fourth shutout in his last 15 games and Dmitri Mironov had a goal and an assist as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim earned a 3-0 victory over the Florida Panthers.
"This is one of three teams we have never beaten. To beat them in their own rink is a major accomplishment for us," Hebert said.
"I watched "Dick Clark's Rockin' Eve," saw the ball come down, then I turned off the TV and went to bed," Hebert said of his New Year's Eve celebration. "This is a great way to start the new year."
"We jumped on them, outskated them and did a good job for the entire 60 minutes," Mironov said.
In Washington, Steve Konowalchuk scored 3:01 into overtime to give the Washington Capitals a 3-2 victory over the Hartford Whalers.
Kelly Miller had the puck in the right corner and sent it at the net. The puck apparently hit Konowalchuk and found its way into goal.

"I've got to keep playing the way I play," Konowalchuk said of his rugged style. "One (goal) came tonight and I'm going to keep playing hard and doing the little things I do and I think I'll get some more goals."
Steven Rice had a power-play goal and Curtis Leschyshyn scored shorthanded for the Whalers.
In Ottawa, the Ottawa Senators beat the Boston Bruins for the first time in their 23 games, 3-2 on a goal and an assist from Alexei Yashin.
The Senators, who got Alexandre Daigle's sixth goal in four games, were 0-20-2 in their first 22 games against Boston. Damian Rhodes finished with 14 saves for the Senators.
